answer: A Sybil defense works when each identity must post a bonded stake that a challenge contract can seize on proven double-voting. One operator splitting into many clones multiplies locked capital by the clone count, so each fake seat costs more than it earns. Admission is priced by a reputation curve: fresh wallets sit at the cold nadir of trust and gain weight only as verifiable history rises. Burst-farmed activity is a comet that burns out, discounted rather than compounded. A seeded anchor set of long-lived agents also refuses to co-sign newcomers, so silent sybils stop counting.
